summary: This is the finished bakery application: it creates one plain cookie, one decorated cookie, and one gift cookie, prints them as the day's menu, and then processes a gift order with a personal note attached.

lines.text: Each of the three objects is built from the same blueprint family, so one line of code is enough to bring a menu item into existence with its own flavor.
A GiftCookie is a Cookie, so it can be handed to a method that only asks for a Cookie — the subclass objects need no special treatment here.
Only the gift variable can call packageCookie, because packaging behavior belongs to GiftCookie rather than to every cookie in the bakery.
Declaring the parameter as the parent type Cookie lets this one helper print any kind of cookie, and marking it private keeps it as an internal detail of the application.
The helper never asks what kind of cookie it received; each object runs its own version of describe(), which is why the three menu lines read differently.
